transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My mind keeps jumping to every little thing around me, and I can’t stay focused on what I’m supposed to be doing anymore. It's gotten to the point where I just can't keep my head straight at work, and I really need to figure out how to get my focus back.
Do you often feel anxious or worried, or is it more about not being able to concentrate and being easily distracted?

I actually started reading up on mental health because I thought I was just anxious, but the overwhelming issue right now is definitely this extreme distractibility. My mind constantly jumps to every little thing around me—like a phone notification or a bird flying by the window—and it completely derails me from finishing whatever task I was working on.
Do you also experience restlessness or fidgeting, or feel like you're constantly 'on the go' even when you're not supposed to be, in addition to the distractibility you're describing?

Yes, absolutely, I feel exactly like that. Most days I can't sit still, like there's a motor running inside me that just won't shut off. I'm constantly jumping from one thing to the next, whether it's rushing out to chase sales leads, starting woodworking projects in the garage, or editing photos late into the night.

Do you often act on impulse, such as interrupting others, blurting out answers, or doing things without much thought, and have you noticed this behavior causing problems in your daily life or relationships?

I definitely talk a mile a minute and tend to snap at my wife and boss when they question me, which has really strained my relationships. While I don't think I constantly interrupt people, I absolutely do things without thinking, like impulsively buying expensive photography and woodworking gear on credit cards. That has made my wife furious and caused some serious financial stress at home.
Can you tell me more about when these symptoms started and if they've been present consistently throughout your life, or if they've developed more recently?

These symptoms aren't lifelong; they actually started ramping up about seven months ago when I transitioned from long-haul truck driving to my new regional sales job. I've had normal ups and downs in the past, but this intense level of energy, distractibility, and mood swings is definitely a recent thing connected to this job change.

You mentioned these symptoms started about seven months ago with your job change; can you tell me if you experienced any similar patterns of behavior or difficulties during your childhood or teenage years, even if they were less severe?

No, I don't recall experiencing anything like this during my childhood or teenage years. These difficulties really only started becoming a major issue for me after my job transition about seven months ago.
Did you exhibit any symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, or impulsivity prior to the age of 12, which might have been less noticeable or problematic at the time?
No, I don't recall having those kinds of attention or hyperactivity issues when I was a kid or before the age of 12. School and growing up seemed pretty normal for me in that regard.

Do you find that these symptoms of restlessness, distractibility, and impulsivity occur in multiple settings, such as at work, at home, and in social situations, or are they mainly confined to one particular setting?

Yes, it's definitely happening in multiple settings, especially at work and at home. At work, I've nearly lost a major client, my boss has warned me about my erratic schedule, and I've been clashing with my manager. At home, I'm constantly snapping at my wife, missing family obligations, and running up credit cards on gear for projects I can't seem to finish.

Given that you've mentioned these symptoms started around seven months ago with your job change and you don't recall similar issues in your childhood, can you think of any specific factors or events related to your job transition that might have triggered or significantly exacerbated these symptoms?

The move from structured long-haul driving to regional sales gave me a lot of freedom but also the pressure of commission-based income and building a client list from scratch. At first, that looser schedule and independence felt incredibly exciting, triggering a huge surge of energy and big ideas for work and side businesses. But eventually, that excitement just spiraled into the disorganized and overwhelming state I'm in now.

You mentioned that these symptoms started about seven months ago, but I'd like to clarify: are you certain that you didn't exhibit any signs of inattention, hyperactivity, or impulsivity during your adolescence or early adulthood, even if they were mild or not as disruptive as what you're experiencing now?

I really don't think I had those kinds of attention or hyperactivity issues when I was younger or in early adulthood. I always managed to get by just fine back then. It wasn't until about seven months ago when I switched to this new sales job that everything started spiraling and became a real problem.

Are you experiencing significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life due to these symptoms, and do you think these issues would persist even if you were to change jobs or environments again?

Yes, it's causing massive problems—I nearly lost a major client, my boss has warned me about my erratic hours, and my wife is furious that I'm missing family events and racking up credit card debt. I actually switched from long-haul driving to this sales job hoping a change would help, but things only got worse, which makes me realize this issue is in my own head and would follow me anywhere.

You've mentioned that these symptoms started about seven months ago, but considering your recent reflections, are you completely sure that there weren't any milder signs of inattention, hyperactivity, or impulsivity in your adolescence or early adulthood that might have been overlooked or not as disruptive?
I honestly don't recall having those kinds of attention or hyperactivity issues when I was younger. As far as I can remember, my focus and energy were completely fine until this recent job change.
Can you describe any instances where you had to work or study in a quiet, structured environment for an extended period, and if so, how you managed your focus and restlessness in those situations?

I don't really have experience working or studying in a quiet, structured environment like that, especially recently. My previous job was long-haul truck driving, which is obviously very different from an office setting. Right now, I'm struggling so much with restlessness and distractibility that I can't even imagine being able to manage well in a quiet room.

You've consistently stated that these symptoms began around seven months ago with your job change, but I want to clarify one more time: are you absolutely certain there were no signs, no matter how mild, of these attention or hyperactivity issues before this recent job transition?

Yes, I am absolutely certain. During my years of long-haul driving, I never experienced these kinds of attention or hyperactivity issues. This constant jumping around and restlessness really only started and ramped up once I transitioned to the regional sales job seven months ago.

I really don't recall having any of those attention or hyperactivity issues when I was a kid before the age of 12. These problems only started ramping up and causing real trouble for me after my job change seven months ago.

These intense feelings of being constantly on the go and easily distracted have really only become a major, disruptive problem since I transitioned to my new regional sales job seven months ago.

I'm really not sure if going back to long-haul driving would fix this, and besides, I made this move to spend more time with my family, so going back isn't what I want. Plus, I don't know if a structured environment would actually stop my mind from racing and constantly jumping around like it is now.

Yes, I am completely certain that I don't recall having these kinds of attention or hyperactivity issues during my youth or early adulthood. My focus and energy were never a problem back then, and these struggles really only started after my job change seven months ago.

If you were to imagine yourself in a hypothetical situation where you're back in a highly structured and predictable environment, similar to your long-haul truck driving job, do you think your current symptoms of distractibility, restlessness, and impulsivity would diminish significantly, or do you believe they would persist regardless of the environment?

I'm really not sure if going back to a structured job would fix things now. This "motor" inside me feels so strong lately that I'm afraid the restlessness and racing thoughts would just keep going, no matter what environment I'm in.

Can you describe any situations or activities where you feel most in control of your hyperactivity and restlessness, and are there any specific strategies or techniques that help you manage these symptoms, even if only temporarily?

To be honest, I don't really have any situations where I feel in control of the restlessness right now. I haven't found any strategies or techniques that actually help manage it, which is exactly why I finally decided to come in and seek professional help.

Have you experienced any periods in the past seven months where your symptoms of hyperactivity and restlessness significantly improved or worsened in response to specific events, stressors, or changes in your daily routine or environment?

They haven't improved; the restlessness has just gotten worse as the pressure of my new sales job mounted over the last seven months. Things really hit a breaking point recently after I nearly lost a major client, got warned by my boss, and had a huge argument with my wife over the credit card debt I ran up buying woodworking and photography gear.
